title: Insert, minimum and maximum
summary: Predict where a new key goes, and find the smallest and largest keys.

hook.goal: Predict the tree that results from inserting keys, and find its minimum and maximum keys.

scenario.title: Adding a contact
scenario.text: You add a new contact to your phone. The search from Lesson 2 must still be able to find it. Where should it go?
scenario.recall: In a price list stored as a BST, do you need to look at every price to find the cheapest?

warmUp.question: In tree T, where does a search for 45 stop?

options.text: At the empty right side of 40
options.reply: Yes: 50, 30, 40, then the right side of 40 is empty. Keep that spot in mind.
A search only stops at an equal key or an empty spot. 45 is larger than 40, so it goes right.

options.text: At the empty left side of 60
options.reply: 45 is smaller than 50, so the search never goes right of the root.

explore.prompt: Where did your key have to go for the search to find it?

options.text: Exactly where the search for it ends: the empty spot it reaches
options.reply: Yes. Insert is search, plus one new leaf where the search stops.

options.text: Anywhere along the bottom of the tree
options.reply: Only one bottom spot works: the one the search reaches.
40 is close to 45, but only one side of it works. Which side did the search reach?

pages.title: Insert
steps: When you reach an empty spot, put a new node there.
Inserting a key that is already in the tree changes nothing.
pages.caption: Inserting 45 follows the search path 50, 30, 40.

pages.title: Minimum and maximum
steps: Minimum: go left until there is no left child.
Maximum: go right until there is no right child.
The minimum can have a right child, so it is not always a leaf.

items.prompt: Insert {10} into this tree. Where does it go?

hints.text: First search for {10}, as if you were looking for it.
The empty spot where the search for {10} stops is marked. That is where a new node goes.

items.explanation: Searching for {10} visits {path} and stops at the empty {side} side of {endAt}, so {10} becomes the {side} child of {endAt}.
items.misconception: Thinking new keys go at the root, or that inserting moves existing nodes.

items.explanation: Searching for {55} visits {path} and stops at the empty {side} side of {endAt}, so {55} becomes the {side} child of {endAt}.
items.misconception: Thinking new keys go at the root, or that inserting moves existing nodes.

items.prompt: Insert {50} into this tree again. What happens?

options: Nothing changes: duplicates are not added
A second {50} becomes the left child of {50}
The tree is rebuilt from the start

hints.text: First search for {50}. Where does the search end?
The search finds {50} straight away at the root.

items.explanation: Nothing changes. The search finds the key, and this app does not allow duplicate keys.

items.prompt: Build a BST by inserting {40}, {20}, {60}, {10} in that order.

hints.text: The first key becomes the root. Then search for each new key before placing it.
{40} is the root. {20} is smaller, so it goes left. Where do {60} and {10} go?

items.explanation: Root {40}; left child {20} with left child {10}; right child {60}.
items.misconception: Thinking new keys go at the root, or that inserting moves existing nodes.

items.prompt: Click the minimum key, then the maximum key.

hints.text: You do not need to compare anything. Which direction leads to smaller keys?
The far-left and far-right paths are highlighted.

items.explanation: Minimum {min} (go left until you cannot). Maximum {max} (go right until you cannot).
items.misconception: Thinking the minimum must be a leaf.

items.prompt: Click the smallest key in the subtree rooted at {70}.

hints.text: Start at {70}. Which way leads to smaller keys?
From {70}, the path going left is highlighted.

items.explanation: {min}: from {70}, go left until there is no left child.
